The quick menu navigates only through an onchange handler. Users who cannot operate the control with a pointer or whose browser does not fire the change event as expected may be unable to navigate.
The page's main title is a paragraph styled to look like a heading rather than a heading element, so the content hierarchy is not programmatically conveyed.
Layout tables are used to arrange page content, which can cause assistive technologies to announce unnecessary table structure and make the layout harder to understand.
The black headline text on the light gray background has a contrast ratio of approximately 4.0:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum for normal-sized text.
The image-only navigation links have no text alternatives; their images are missing alt attributes, leaving the links without accessible names.
The navigation links call blur() on focus, removing keyboard focus and disrupting the expected focus order and operation.
The current News Page item is an anchor without an href, so it is not a functional link despite being presented as one.
The fixed-width 800px and 780px layout tables are likely to require horizontal scrolling at narrow viewport widths, impairing reflow.
The navigation links explicitly blur on focus, preventing users from seeing which link has keyboard focus.
The quick-menu select has no associated label or accessible name explaining its purpose.
